title: Identifying Paired-Propensity Mixtures and Risk-Difference Distributions from Crossover Profile Tables
banked_reason: D0.5.G delivered tier=subfield below the field floor: the complete arbitrary-menu characterization is sound and fully discharged, but exact-population known-r scope without estimation, inference, conditioning, or robustness caps significance at subfield.
gap_reasons: The result is confined to exact population injectivity for a known finite atom bound under stable, conditionally independent Bernoulli responses, and it supplies no estimator, conditioning analysis, uncertainty quantification, or robustness to carryover, drift, and residual dependence.
The identified causal distribution concerns class-average propensity differences rather than individual binary potential-outcome contrasts, which materially narrows its causal interpretation.
D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 6.5 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'field' is capped at 'subfield'.
proof_attempt_summary: The run proved and fully discharged the exact hyperbolic-cross criterion, positive at-most-r target-distinguishing twins, the endpoint/adjacent-gap menu test, and complete unrestricted and all-crossover impossible/three/two/one-profile frontiers. The primary van Wieringen comparison was resolved from the supplied article and the strict-subclass/non-transfer positioning survived both substantive D0.5 panels. Nothing mathematical collapsed; the package was downgraded because the cold referee judged its exact-population, known-r scope intrinsically subfield rather than field, with estimation, inference, conditioning, and robustness requiring a new project.
tldr: Under randomized supported assignment, stable conditionally independent Bernoulli responses, and a positive mixing law with at most \(r\) atoms, the observed profile tables identify the full paired-propensity law exactly when their moment staircase contains \(H_{2r}\). Explicit positive finite-difference twins show that every failure also destroys identification of the risk-difference distribution and beneficial-class mass. The resulting endpoint-and-adjacent-gap test yields two exact design frontiers: unrestricted menus require respectively infinity, three, two, or one profiles as periods cross \(2r-1\), \(\tau_2(r)\), and \(4r-2\); when pure profiles are forbidden, the first threshold shifts to \(2r\), while the later thresholds are unchanged. At \(T=2r\), two all-crossover profiles suffice exactly for \(r=2,3,4\), and otherwise three are minimum. The novelty claim is limited to the incomplete-menu positive-law converse, its causal pushforwards, and these menu characterizations; the full-support grouped-mixture and hyperbolic-cross ingredients are credited prior art.
gap: Sauer already supplies the universal hyperbolic-cross interpolation engine, and general product-binomial and grouped-mixture theory supplies important sufficient or worst-case results. Van Wieringen (2005), Theorem 2 on PDF p. 3, already gives a sufficient condition for a separated two-latent-class model observed through one complete product-binomial table, and Remark 6 on PDF p. 7 explicitly says its coordinatewise separation condition is not necessary. What remains unsupported by the inspected theorem text is the positive at-most-\(r\) probability-law converse that changes the risk-difference pushforward and beneficial mass for every failed incomplete menu, together with a necessary-and-sufficient arbitrary-menu criterion, the endpoint/adjacent-gap characterization, and the exact crossover design frontier. This is a bounded difference from inspected sources, not a field-priority claim.
fill: Prove explicit positive finite-difference twins for every omitted required moment and show that they change both causal targets; then use the credited interpolation criterion and the Bernstein-staircase translation to derive the endpoint-and-adjacent-gap test, the exact period/profile frontier, and the all-crossover boundary.
